title: No VIP Left Behind: ECI’s Drive to Guarantee a Spot For Them on the Final Voter Roll
authors: Ayushi Kar, Shubhangi Derhgawen, Sumedha Mittal, Dikshya Koirala
shows: Reports that the Delhi revision gave people the Commission treated as VIPs a separate route onto the roll, through a 'Mark VIP' module in the booth-level officers' app, WhatsApp groups and orders. Ordinary electors with notices were sent to queues and hearings.

title: UP CEO Confirms: 16.18 Lakh Applications for Addition Accepted Before Draft Roll. Falsely Claims Details Were Hidden on ECI’s Instructions
shows: Follows the earlier report on 16.18 lakh additions in Uttar Pradesh. The state's Chief Electoral Officer confirmed the Form 6 applications were taken before the draft roll and said their details were withheld on the Commission's instructions, and the report sets that against Commission instructions requiring applications after the draft and public details.

title: Delhi SIR: ECI Forcing BLOs to Sign Off on Voters Without Verification
shows: Reports that booth-level officers in Delhi were told over WhatsApp to clear electors flagged for 'logical discrepancies' by signing a new 'certificate' form. Under this route the flagged cases are closed with no documents and no hearing.

title: Special drive in States/UTs after completion of Special Intensive Revision (SIR) – reg. (Letter No. 23/2025/ERS(Vol-II))
shows: The Commission's letter to all Chief Electoral Officers ordering a drive to enrol left-out and young electors. Booth-level officers are to compare the current roll with the pre-SIR roll, list everyone missing, visit each house within about a month, help eligible people fill Form 6 and share the lists with party agents.

title: Press Note (No. ECI/PN/121/2026)
shows: Records a Commission meeting attended by all three Commissioners that extended the SIR in Andhra Pradesh (claims and notices to 10 October, final roll on 16 October) and moved Meghalaya's final roll to 26 October 2026.

title: SIR Draft Rolls Show Highest Voter Deletions in States Where Elections Were Held in Last 3 Years
shows: Tabulates the phase 3 draft rolls, 6.15 crore names left off across 17 states and UTs. The five states with the most names left off (Maharashtra, Karnataka, Telangana, Delhi, Andhra Pradesh) all held Assembly elections between 2023 and 2025, and the lowest shares were in Mizoram, Odisha, Manipur, Meghalaya and Sikkim.

title: Bengaluru to Lucknow, why urban centres are seeing high electoral roll deletions during SIR
shows: Compares the district with the highest share of names left off in several states: the Bengaluru districts in Karnataka (43 to 49 per cent), Lucknow in Uttar Pradesh, Surat in Gujarat, Chennai in Tamil Nadu, Bhopal in Madhya Pradesh, Gurugram and Hyderabad. Two former Election Commissioners explain the pattern by migration, and one says deletions for failing to map to the 2002-03 roll would be unfair.

title: Explainer: Why fewer voters were deleted in Odisha compared to several other states
shows: Sets Odisha's net fall of 17.67 lakh (about 5.3 per cent) from the pre-SIR roll to the final roll of 21 September against other states. It gives a 94 per cent return of enumeration forms, few duplicates and mostly seasonal migration as the reasons, and explains how a deleted elector can appeal or reapply.

title: Amid elector apathy, EC extends Maharashtra SIR deadline yet again till October 26
shows: Gives the reasons behind Maharashtra's 2.07 crore names left off the draft (7.68 million shifted, 7.55 million absent, 3.48 million dead, 1.76 million duplicates). By 12 October only 8.33 lakh applications and 25,661 Form 7 objections had come in, and 1.22 crore electors on the draft were flagged as unmapped or discrepant.

title: SIR: Telangana may witness net deletion of 70 lakh names or more from electoral rolls
shows: Reports that Telangana's draft of 17 August left off more than 73 lakh electors while fresh enrolment applications stayed under 5 lakh, so the net fall may reach 70 lakh. The Chief Electoral Officer's figures show more than 10.2 lakh claims and objections received by 7 October.

title: After SIR, 13.4% deletions in Gujarat electoral rolls
authors: Abhishek Jha, Maulik Pathak, Harsh Yadav
shows: Reads Gujarat's final roll of 4.40 crore against the pre-SIR roll, a net fall of 13.4 per cent. The largest falls were in Surat, Ahmedabad and Vadodara and the smallest in the tribal districts of Dang, Chhota Udepur and Narmada.

title: Analysis and Explainer on the Software of the SIR That Runs Without Transparency
shows: Describes the systems behind the revision (ECINET, the BLO app, ERONET run by TCS since 2023, the mapping and 'logical discrepancy' rules, machine transliteration and duplicate-detection tools) and finds none has a published specification, threshold or audit. It counts 1.31 crore electors flagged in West Bengal and 2.35 crore in Madhya Pradesh by the discrepancy rules.

title: Powers of the CEC | Day 1: SC seeks ECI’s response on plea
shows: Reports the hearing in which the Court issued notice to the Commission and all three Commissioners on petitions alleging the Chief Election Commissioner took decisions alone, and declined to suspend him in the interim. The Chief Justice said no modified Form 6 had been approved by the Court.

title: ‘Do not put words in our mouth’: Supreme Court says it never adjudicated new Form 6, will examine challenge on Oct 27
shows: Reports the bench clarifying that it neither approved nor disapproved the declaration added to Form 6, because it did not exist when the Bihar judgment was given. It sets out the Commission's 26 September claim, the rule-making route under Section 28 of the 1950 Act, and the listing of the challenge for 27 October.

title: Supreme Court wants cases of SIR excluded to be decided before next polls. A reality check from Assam
shows: Sets the Supreme Court's direction that exclusions be decided before the next polls against Assam's record. About 3 lakh voters were marked 'Doubtful' in a 1997 revision and 93,000 'D' voters remained before the 2026 Assembly election, with cases held up in Foreigners Tribunals and courts.

title: Gyanesh Kumar Row: How did the ECI delete 13 crore voters during the SIR | Insight India
shows: A conversation with The Hindu's Srinivasan Ramani on how more than 13 crore names came off draft rolls in 30 states and UTs, what the data says about who was left off, and the questions about the exercise's legality.

title: Focus on inclusion made Kerala SIR credible | Onmanorama Explains
shows: Walks through Kerala's figures: the final roll is 8,97,211 below the 2024 roll (3.24 per cent), more than 98 per cent of the 36.89 lakh unmapped or discrepant electors were kept after hearings, and 92.7 per cent of 14.57 lakh Form 6 applications were accepted. Booth-level officers told the channel they were asked to include as many voters as possible.

title: Election Commission Investigation: Ritika Chopra Answers All Your Questions On ECI Investigation
shows: The editor who led the paper's investigation into the two Commissioners' objections answers readers' questions: how the software-made 'logical discrepancy' category works, why objections on file by two of three members matter under the law, and what the Commission's reply did and did not deny.
